title: The key rings? I love them!
grammar: Object pronouns: it, them, him, her, us
pair_game: Point at a picture. Ask: “Do you like them?” Your partner answers with it or them. Then swap!

grammar_box.title: I love them!
grammar_box.tip: The object pronoun comes AFTER the verb: I love them. (NOT I them love.)

questions: Do you like key rings or collect things?
What do you love to do after school?
Do you hate getting up early in the morning?
What is your favorite thing in your room?
Do you like dogs or cats more?
Who do you love the most in your family?
Do you like playing soccer or video games more?
What don't you like about school?
Do you love your new shoes or clothes?
Tell me something you really like or love.
starters: Yes, I collect … . I love **them**! / No, I do not collect anything.
Yes, I hate it! / No, I do not mind, because … .
My favourite thing in my room is … . I love **it** because … .
I love my … the most, because … .
I like … more. I play **it** … times a week.
I do not like … at school, because … .
Yes, I love **them**! / No, I do not have new shoes.
I really love … . I … **it/them** every day.
samples: Do you like key rings or collect things?
Yes! I collect key rings. I have twenty-six and I love **them**. My cousin sends me one from every city.
What is your favorite thing in your room?
My favourite thing is my old teddy bear. My grandmother gave **him** to me and I keep **him** on my bed.
What don't you like about school?
I do not like the long lessons on Friday. I find **them** boring, but I like the breaks!

game.title: Spin and say!
game.rules: Spin the pencil. Say two sentences about the topic. Use it, them, him or her!

mini_talk.title: My favourite things
plan: Say what you collect or love
Say what you do not like
mini_talk.model: I collect stickers and I love **them**! I have more than one hundred and I keep **them** in a big blue book. I like **them** because every sticker is from a different city. My favourite thing in my room is my lamp — my father made **it** for me. I do not like computer games. I think **they** are boring, so I never play **them**.

cando: use it, them, him and her after verbs
talk about things I love and hate
